data.narrative:
Silicon Quantum Computing is a Series A quantum computing company that has raised A$83M to date, founded by Michelle Simmons. The quantum computing sector includes a peer universe of 11 companies (3 public: IonQ, Rigetti Computing, D-Wave Systems; 8 private including Quantinuum, PsiQuantum, and SandboxAQ), though a narrow peer-median approach proved inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the sector—fewer than three datapoints met valuation-tier and stage filters.

Valuation analysis relied on stage-progression methodology, which applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement to the A$83M raised proxy, yielding an implied valuation of $166M. This represents the single quantifiable anchor available given the sparse and heterogeneous quantum computing peer set at comparable maturity stages.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $141M (low) to $191M (high) centered on $166M (median). Key uncertainties include the lack of narrow-stage peer validation, the nascent and fragmented nature of the quantum computing market, and the wide dispersion in development approaches and commercial maturity across the identified peer set. The single-method triangulation and absence of revenue or near-term commercialization milestones in the provided dataset further constrain confidence in precision beyond the stated range.
